Play the people you actually like.

Not a club ladder full of strangers. Your own group, your own competition, and a reason to see each other every week.

EffePadelle. Free on the App Store and Google Play.

#EffePadelle #padelfriends #padelgroup #padelleague #padelseason #padel #padelapp #padelnederland #padelcompetitie #padellife #padeltime #padelplayer #padellovers #padelclub #padelcommunity #padelcompetition #padelbelgie

Our group chat had been trying to plan padel since the summer. Nobody ever said no. We just never landed on an evening.

So one of us set up a casual competition in the app instead of chasing one night. Everyone plays everyone once, at their own pace, no end date to miss.

One link in the chat. Eight people in. The app builds the rounds, shows the evenings nobody is busy, and keeps the standings up to date after you type in the sets.

We've played every week since. The chat is louder than it's been in two years.

Swipe to see how it works. Search EffePadelle in the App Store or on Google Play. Free to start.

Top half is a photo we took on the recce. Bottom half is what ended up in the edit.

We shot the whole location on our phones a few weeks before the shoot. Framing, lens, where the lamp stands, where the actor sits. Then we tick it off one by one on the day.

It's a bit much, sure. But it means nobody is standing in a living room at 8am wondering where to put the camera. By the time the crew walks in, most of it is already decided.

Three films, no shooting day.

A campaign we made up ourselves, to show what we can do with a campaign made entirely with AI. There's no client. We wrote the scripts ourselves, and every image after that was generated.

This is all three in one. The next three days, one each: the police officers, the gardener and the terrace.

rokufilms.com

#rokufilms #aifilm #aicommercial #generativeai #aivideo #speccommercial #commercialproduction #filmproduction #creativeproduction #advertising #brandfilm #productioncompany #amsterdam #scriptwriting

The police officers.

The first of three films from our fictional AI campaign. We wrote the script the way we'd write one for a shoot. Every frame after that was made with AI.

That doesn't mean you type a sentence and this comes out. You need to know what you're after and how to ask for it, and then you still throw most of it away.

robert@rokufilms.com

#rokufilms #aifilm #aicommercial #generativeai #aivideo #speccommercial #commercialproduction #filmproduction #creativeproduction #advertising #brandfilm #productioncompany #amsterdam #scriptwriting

The gardener.

Film two. Same way of working as the others: first the script, written by us, then the images, made with AI shot by shot until they matched what was on the page.

No crew, no location, no shooting day. For some campaign films that makes them simpler and faster to make.

rokufilms.com

#rokufilms #aifilm #aicommercial #generativeai #aivideo #speccommercial #commercialproduction #filmproduction #creativeproduction #advertising #brandfilm #productioncompany #amsterdam #scriptwriting

The terrace.

The last of the three. A fictional campaign: no client and nothing shot. The scripts are ours, the images were made with AI.

AI is going to be a big part of how films get made. It still doesn't hand you a result like this on its own. The script, knowing what to ask for, and choosing what to keep: that's the work.

Curious what this could mean for your project? Send us a message.

We like getting the call early.

If we're there while the script is still being written, we can tell you early what will be hard to shoot, and what will cost more than it looks. That saves a lot of trouble later.

Why a bingo hall.

The script needed three everyday moments of luck. A parking space that opens up right in front of you. Being next in a long queue at the supermarket. And a third one that points at the casino itself.

Bingo is about the most recognisable game of luck there is, so the last scene went there.

The art department cleaned the car park as well as it could be cleaned, and painted the seven on the ground. In post we still spent hours taking stains out of the asphalt.

The cars were a job of their own. From up there you see every car at once, so red, grey and black had to be parked in exactly the right spots.
